claim: md1dsp (MT6785 modem DSP) ISA is byte-testable with the same decode-density method that closed md1rom; the rosemary census's Coresonic-class attribution and F-17's 'DSP! magic, ISA not decodable' flag are testable
verdict: md1dsp is the modem L1/PHY DSP firmware whose build tree self-identifies the core as MediaTek MD32 (122 source-path strings 'md32/usip/...', 'md32/rake/...'); instruction-level decode is an honest negative: no available decoder produces coherent code (6 languages tested: MIPS32, MIPS16e, microMIPS, nanoMIPS, Xtensa, stock-Ghidra MD32 - max 6.25% on non-artifact windows vs 88-100.8% for md1rom islands)

input.census_crosscheck: rosemary-census.json partitions/6/records: md1dsp size 6783260, offset 28058992, mtk_hdr hdr_size 512 - size matches exactly
input.container: 512-B mtk_hdr (FILE_INFO: payload 0x678000 bytes at file offset 0x118) + DSP! image header: magic 'DSP!' at 0x118, +0x0C size 0x678000, +0x10 version 1, +0x18 marker 0x12345678, +0x1C chip 'MT6785', +0x2C 'DEFAULT_ASIC', +0xAC build string

method.tool: Ghidra 12.2 PUBLIC headless (cold-start: no auto-analysis, forced disassembly per window)
languages_tested: MD32:LE:32:default (stock Ghidra 'MediaTek MD32' - chosen AFTER strings revealed the md32 build tree)
method.metric: per 256-byte window: clearListing + forced disassembly from window start; coverage = valid instruction bytes / 256 (F-20/F-28/F-31 decode-density methodology)
window_sets: fine sweep of string-bearing regions 0x60000-0x5dd000 (13 windows, 16e/MIPS32/MD32)
method.artifact_note: pure-zero windows 'decode' exactly 68 bytes in every fixed 32-bit ISA (17 x 4-byte instructions) and 34 x 2-byte under MIPS16e; identical windows also hit 26.56%/13.28% under MD32/16e at data windows containing >=68-B zero runs. These rows are disassembler artifacts on zero runs, not code. Repeating 4-byte data patterns partially decode (e.g. 0x4c0000: 16e 29.69% = alternating 'addiu v1,sp,0x3a0 / addiu s0,sp,0x100' x7 - data, not code).

auto_analysis.note: MIPS32 auto-analysis creates essentially no code - confirming the ISA negative; it does auto-define 15,594 data items including the string evidence below

version_strings: MOLY.LR13.R1.MP.V89.6.P79 (identical to md1rom - same MOLY LR13 build package)

prior_art: cyrozap/mediatek-lte-baseband-re (GitHub) - reverse engineering of the MTK LTE baseband's Coresonic DSP inside the MT6295 modem; establishes that older-generation (MT6295-era) MTK modem DSPs are Coresonic cores
CEVA acquired Coresonic (2014); no open Ghidra/SLEIGH decoder exists for Coresonic/CEVA XC-class vector DSPs
Check Point Research 2021 'Looking for Vulnerabilities in MediaTek Audio DSP' - custom opcodes, unrelated core (HiFi/Xtensa)
census F-16/F-17: md1dsp DSP! container, 'modem DSP = Coresonic-class per cyrozap/NCC DSP symbol history; ISA not decodable'

interpretation.core_id: string-level (strong): the firmware's own assert/build strings place it in the 'md32' source tree - MediaTek's MD32 DSP core (Ghidra 12.2 ships an MD32:LE:32:default processor module, evidently for a different MD32 generation/subsystem use)
interpretation.census_update: the census's 'Coresonic-class' attribution for MT6785 md1dsp is superseded by the self-naming md32 build tree (Coresonic attribution remains valid for the MT6295 generation per cyrozap)
interpretation.isa_negative: the instruction stream does not decode under any of the 6 tested languages (incl. Ghidra's own MD32 module): code regions 0x40000-0xC0000, 0x140000-0x180000, 0x53C000-0x600000 are dense non-zero bytes with 0-6.25% coverage; possible causes: packed/compressed code sections, or an MD32 ISA generation not covered by Ghidra's module
interpretation.family_map: MT6785 modem subsystem uses at least two distinct core families: MIPS32+MIPS16e (md1rom protocol/AP cores) and md32 DSP (md1dsp L1/PHY); audio_dsp HiFi3 Xtensa is a third

limitations: Ghidra MD32 module is stock (no pspec tuning, no load-address knowledge from the DSP! header); a future pass with DSP! segment load addresses or an MD32 ISA variant doc could still close the byte-level decode
no attempt to decompress/pack-detect the 0x600000+ tail (high-entropy, likely compressed secondary image)
auto-analysis run under MIPS32 (no winner language existed); instruction/function counts are therefore not meaningful beyond confirming the negative
window step 256 KiB (main) / ad-hoc (fine) - island boundaries not mapped
